ambiguities: The publication's exact filtering, clustering identity threshold, chimera handling and reference-database version usage were not extracted before termination.
Whether the reported OTU counts refer to the combined data set or per marker (16S vs ITS) separately was not confirmed from the text.
assumptions: The publication describes the method; its own text is the only methodological source permitted.
Served reads under /input/reads and references under /input/references would be the inputs for a faithful reimplementation.
No original implementation, processed OTU table or repository was available, so the filtered-data OTU counts must be recomputed from raw reads.
claimed_report.conclusion: The run was terminated by the harness before any analysis could be executed: the response stream was cut off on length while repeatedly probing the publication text, so no reads were processed and no OTU counts were computed. The target (number of unique bacterial 16S OTUs and fungal ITS OTUs in the filtered data set) was therefore not observed.

ambiguities: The publication's direction labels (5949 down / 813 up) are opposite in sign to the DEGseq log2(3D/2D) convention; the total and the two directional counts are unambiguous, but which direction is called 'up' vs 'down' depends on the reference group. Reported here as in the publication.
The publication text mentions both 'fold change > 2' and '|log2 fold change| >= 1' in different places; these are equivalent and both were applied.
assumptions: DEGseq MARS method used, as the publication states DEGs were screened using Degseq.
Thresholds taken from the publication: fold change > 2 (equivalently |log2 fold change| >= 1), p = 0.05, q (padj) = 0.05.
Counts used as raw read counts with library-size normalization performed internally by DEGseq (depth1=14371084, depth2=16652503).

Direction labels follow the publication: the 5949-gene group is reported as down-regulated and the 813-gene group as up-regulated (in DEGseq output, log2FC = log2(3D/2D); the 5949 group has log2FC > 1 and the 813 group has log2FC < -1).
All 52550 genes present in both count files were used; no additional filtering was applied beyond the published thresholds.
claimed_report.conclusion: Reproduced the published DEG counts for 3D- vs 2D-cultured RAW264.7 macrophages using DEGseq (MARS method) on the two served count files (GSM5662247 2D, GSM5662248 3D), with the published thresholds fold change > 2 (|log2FC| >= 1), p = 0.05 and q/padj = 0.05. Observed total = 6762, with 5949 in one direction and 813 in the other, exactly matching the publication's reported 6762 / 5949 down / 813 up.

ambiguities: The publication does not state the reference category for body condition score; the reported value 0.022 uniquely identifies good vs poor.
The publication reports OR = n/a for several variables and does not describe handling of multi-category variables in the final model.
assumptions: OR computed from the deposited 2x2 contingency tables as the exponentiated logistic-regression coefficient for the single predictor, consistent with the publication's logistic regression analysis.

For body condition score the reference category is 'poor' (coded 0) and the reported OR 0.022 is for 'good' (coded 1) versus 'poor'; the reverse coding gives 45.9, which does not match the publication.
Horse column coding 0=normal, 1=colic as documented in the deposit's legend rows.
Only the two target variables were reconstructed; no alternative specifications were explored.
claimed_report.conclusion: Reconstructed Table 2 odds ratios from the deposited risk-factor dataset (n=115; 96 colic, 19 normal) using the publication's stated method (chi-square screening followed by logistic regression; OR from conditional logistic regression). Previous exposure to colic: 2x2 counts absent 15 normal/10 colic, present 4 normal/86 colic gives OR = (86*15)/(4*10) = 32.25, matching the published 32.250. Body condition score: poor 2 normal/81 colic, good 17 normal/15 colic; the published OR = 0.022 corresponds to good vs poor, OR = (15*2)/(17*81) = 0.02179, matching the published 0.022. Single-predictor logistic regression reproduces both exactly (32.250 and 0.021786).

ambiguities: The publication does not state the exact reference category for each OR; the reported values match the dataset's 0/1 coding directly.
Table 2 lists OR only on one row per variable; the complementary category's OR is its reciprocal.
assumptions: The publication reports OR from logistic regression; the deposited data allow exact univariable logistic regression, which reproduces the published ORs for these two variables.
Coding follows the dataset's own legend: Horse 0=normal, 1=colic; Previous exposure colic 0=absent, 1=present; Body condition score 0=poor, 1=good.
The OR for body condition score is reported for the 'good' category relative to 'poor' (the row carrying the OR in Table 2), giving 0.022.
The 115 data rows (rows 0-114) were used; rows 115-119 are legend/blank rows and were excluded.
SPSS v.25 was the original software; statsmodels Logit was used as the equivalent available implementation.
claimed_report.conclusion: Reconstructed Table 2 odds ratios from the deposited dataset (Risk_factor_in_horse_with_colic.xlsx, sheet 'Risk factor', 115 horses: 96 colic, 19 normal) using univariable logistic regression as described in the publication's Statistical analysis section (Chi-square screening followed by logistic regression; OR reported). Previous exposure to colic: OR = 32.250 (p = 1.11e-07), matching the published Table 2 value of 32.250. Body condition score: OR = 0.022 (p = 1.66e-06), matching the published Table 2 value of 0.022. Both target values are reproduced exactly from the served inputs.

ambiguities: The publication does not state the exact optimizer or convergence criterion used for the least-squares fit; the small kappa_n discrepancy (17242.080 vs 17242.068) is consistent with optimizer tolerance.
The publication does not explicitly define eta_n's estimator; RMS residual was used because it reproduces the published value exactly.
assumptions: Time index t = 1 corresponds to publication year 1981 and t = T = 36 to 2016, as implied by 'n(t) for t in {1,2,...,T}' and the 36-year span 1981-2016.
n(t) is the count of nodes per publication year taken directly from wos-stat_nodes.csv (179483 nodes total, matching the published count).
Least squares was applied to the raw counts n(t) (not to a normalized or floored version), using the logistic mean function f_n.
eta_n is reported as the root-mean-square of the least-squares residuals (sqrt(mean(residual^2))), which reproduces the published value 328.047.
Optimization used scipy.optimize.least_squares (Levenberg-Marquardt) with tight tolerances; no alternative specifications were explored.
claimed_report.conclusion: The published logistic function f_n(t | mu_n, sigma_n, kappa_n) = kappa_n / (1 + exp(-(t - mu_n)/sigma_n)) was fitted by ordinary least squares to the annual paper counts n(t) of WoS-Stat, where t = 1..T indexes publication years 1981..2016 (T = 36) and n(t) is the number of nodes with that publication year in wos-stat_nodes.csv. The reconstruction reproduces the published estimates: mu_n = 33.263, sigma_n = 14.743, kappa_n = 17242.080 (published kappa_n = 17242.068, difference 0.012 attributable to optimizer tolerance), and the residual scale eta_n = 328.047 (RMS of residuals), matching the published eta_n = 328.047.
